articles.title: Nearly 100 fall ill after eating pani puri, tikki from street vendor in UP villages
articles.summary: LUCKNOW: Nearly 100 people, including a large number of children, women and elderly residents, fell ill after allegedly consuming contaminated pani puri
articles.body: LUCKNOW: Nearly 100 people, including a large number of children, women and elderly residents, fell ill after allegedly consuming contaminated pani puri and tikki sold by a street vendor in two villages of Siddharthnagar district.The incident was reported from Pedari and Kalnakhor villages under Khesraha police station limits, triggering panic among residents.The affected people complained of vomiting and diarrhoea within a few hours of consuming the street food. As their condition deteriorated, family members rushed them to Madhav Prasad Tripathi Medical College in Siddharthnagar, where they were admitted and are undergoing treatment.According to preliminary information, a street vendor selling pani puri and tikki had visited the villages on Friday evening. Several villagers, including children and elderly people, purchased and consumed the food.However, within hours, people from multiple families started experiencing symptoms of food poisoning, including vomiting and loose motions.The sudden outbreak led to a rush of patients to the medical college, with nearly 100 people reportedly affected.A villager, Yogendra, said several people in the locality fell ill after consuming food purchased from the vendor. The situation worsened as more residents began reporting similar symptoms.Ashish Maurya, whose sister was among those affected, said she had eaten pani puri from the street vendor on Friday evening. She suddenly developed vomiting and diarrhoea during the night, following which the family rushed her to the medical college.“Her condition deteriorated suddenly after she complained of vomiting and loose motions. We immediately brought her to the medical college. She is feeling better now, but her treatment is continuing,” he said.Another victim, Chandni, said she had also consumed pani puri from the vendor and subsequently fell ill. She is currently admitted to the hospital and receiving treatment.Vijay Kumar, another affected resident, said he developed vomiting and loose motions shortly after returning home following his evening meal of pani puri. He subsequently reached the medical college for treatment and has experienced some relief.Dr Bilal Ahmed, who is posted in the emergency ward of Siddharthnagar Medical College, said patients from villages under Khesraha police station had been brought to the hospital after consuming pani puri and tikki.According to him, around 35 to 36 children were among those admitted to the medical college. Three children were initially in a critical condition, but their health improved following treatment and they are now stable.All the patients are being treated and kept under medical observation.Dr Ahmed said the exact cause of the food poisoning was yet to be established. Investigations would be required to determine whether the contamination originated from the water used in preparing pani puri or the chickpea-based filling and other ingredients.Taking cognisance of the incident, Siddharthnagar Chief Medical Officer (CMO) Sanjay Dohre visited the affected villages and took stock of the situation. He said health department teams had been deployed immediately after receiving information about the outbreak.According to the CMO, preliminary information suggested that the street vendor might have served residents leftover boiled potatoes and other food ingredients from the previous night. Their consumption is suspected to have triggered the outbreak, although the actual cause is yet to be confirmed.He said the health department had mobilised medical teams in the morning to identify affected residents and provide treatment. Patients whose condition was relatively serious were referred to Siddharthnagar Medical College for specialised care.The CMO clarified that no deaths had been reported so far and that all affected patients were being closely monitored.Medical teams from Khesraha Community Health Centre (CHC) and the Uska Bazar area, along with other health department personnel, have been deployed in the affected villages to provide medical assistance.Dohre said the situation was currently under control, with the health department maintaining surveillance over the affected population.Meanwhile, medical teams at the medical college and health department personnel stationed in the villages are continuing treatment and monitoring of the affected residents.The incident has triggered concern among villagers, particularly as nearly 100 people from two villages reportedly developed similar symptoms after consuming food purchased from the same street vendor.While preliminary inputs have pointed towards the possible use of leftover food ingredients, officials said the precise source of contamination would be established only after an investigation.The health department is monitoring the situation to prevent further cases and ensure that all affected residents receive timely medical attention.You Can Also Check: Gold Rate in Lucknow | Silver Rate in Lucknow | Bank Holidays in Lucknow | Public Holidays in Lucknow | Lucknow AQI | Weather in Lucknow | Petrol Price in Lucknow | Diesel Price in Lucknow | CNG Price in Lucknow | LPG Price in LucknowStay updated with the latest Lucknow news. articles.title: A New Jersey supermarket sold the winning ticket for an $847 million Powerball jackpot and received a $30,000 retailer bonus; instead of keeping it, the store said the money would go to a food bank
articles.summary: A single lottery ticket sold at a New Jersey supermarket matched all the winning numbers to claim an $847 million Powerball jackpot.
articles.body: A single lottery ticket sold at a New Jersey supermarket matched all the winning numbers to claim an $847 million Powerball jackpot. The win ended a run of 35 drawings without a jackpot winner. The winning numbers drawn on Wednesday evening, 4 November 2026, were white balls 15, 34, 41, 53 and 56, with red Powerball 21 and a Power Play multiplier of 2X. According to the New Jersey Lottery, the winning ticket was sold at Wegmans Food Market, located at 100 Farm View in Montvale, Bergen County. The supermarket will receive a $30,000 bonus from state lottery officials for selling the winning ticket. However, the store will not keep the money. Wegmans confirmed that the full $30,000 will be donated to the Community FoodBank of New Jersey through its Check Out Hunger campaign. The prize is the ninth-largest jackpot in Powerball history.Ticket purchased at self-service terminalAccording to store manager Nick Tassi, who spoke to CBS New York, the winning ticket was bought on Tuesday morning, before the draw, using one of the supermarket's self-service lottery machines. As of Thursday afternoon, no one had come forward to claim the prize. Under a New Jersey law passed in 2020, lottery winners can keep their identities private indefinitely. This means the public may never find out who won the jackpot. The winner can choose between receiving the full $847 million as an annuity over 29 years, paid in 30 increasing instalments, or taking an immediate cash payment of $363.1 million. Both amounts are before federal and state taxes. "Congratulations to our newest New Jersey winner," said New Jersey Lottery Commission Chair Ian Leonard in an official statement released by the state lottery office.Retailer bonus redirected to hunger reliefWegmans' decision to donate its $30,000 retailer bonus means the winning ticket will also provide immediate help to the local community, even if the winner does not come forward straight away. The donation will be made through the company's annual Check Out Hunger campaign. The campaign runs across Wegmans stores and raises money for local hunger-relief groups, including the Community FoodBank of New Jersey. The Community FoodBank of New Jersey is the state's largest organisation fighting hunger. It distributes food and provides support services across 15 of New Jersey's 21 counties. Lottery officials also pointed out that ticket sales provide significant funding for public services. According to the New Jersey Lottery Commission's official statement, lottery proceeds have contributed almost $35.7 billion to public programmes since 1970. Under a 30-year agreement signed by the state in 2017, the lottery's net proceeds go directly towards the public employee pension system.Scale of the Wednesday drawingThe $847 million win is the second jackpot worth more than $1 billion in 2026, following a $1.04 billion Powerball prize won in Illinois on 12 August. According to figures released by Powerball, the biggest jackpot in the game's history remains the $2.04 billion prize won in California in November 2022. Millions of smaller prizes were also won across the country in Wednesday's drawing. These were awarded to ticket holders who matched some, but not all, of the winning numbers. After the jackpot was won, the advertised prize for the next Saturday drawing returned to $20 million. State lottery officials have advised anyone who bought a ticket for the 4 November drawing to check their numbers carefully. They also recommend signing the back of any winning ticket straight away. Winners in New Jersey have up to one year from the draw date to claim their prizes.You use AI every day. Now get your AI Quotient. Take the AIQ test.

articles.title: Watch: Sonia, Priyanka take a trip down memory lane, recall Diwali with Rajiv Gandhi
articles.summary: NEW DELHI: Veteran Congress leader Sonia Gandhi and her daughter, Priyanka Gandhi, revisited memories of Diwali celebrations with former prime minister
articles.body: NEW DELHI: Veteran Congress leader Sonia Gandhi and her daughter, Priyanka Gandhi, revisited memories of Diwali celebrations with former prime minister Rajiv Gandhi.In a conversation shared on social media, Sonia Gandhi recalled her fondness for Diwali, describing the elaborate decorations, traditional rituals and festive gatherings that marked the celebrations."Oh, Diwali I loved. So, Diwali was always beautiful," she recalled in a video shared on her Instagram account.Recalling the traditional rituals, Sonia said a Ganesh idol was placed at the entrance of the house, where the first diya of the celebrations was lit. She added that the idol is now kept at her residence."At the entrance, there used to be a Ganesh Murti, which is now in my house. And so, we would do the first lighting of the diya in front of Ganesh Ji's Murti. And it was always decorated. In those days, we didn't have those little lights everywhere, but we had diyas everywhere - around the pond, all along the roof, veranda, and along the path, wherever there was a path. So, it was very pretty," she said.Priyanka Gandhi, the MP from Wayanad, also recalled how festivals were celebrated with great enthusiasm, with people from different walks of life gathering in the Gandhi family's garden.Sonia remembered how the family would sometimes get carried away with firecrackers, while Priyanka recalled how her father, Rajiv Gandhi, would take them to Chandni Chowk in Old Delhi to buy crackers."Papa used to take us to Chandni Chowk to buy crackers. We used to go to Old Delhi to buy crackers," Priyanka recalled.Sonia also remembered phuljhadis, or traditional sparklers, saying she enjoyed them, although she was less enthusiastic about some of the noisier fireworks.Beyond the lights and firecrackers, Sonia said the atmosphere during the festive season remained particularly memorable. Recalling the weather during those celebrations, she spoke about the clear blue skies that formed the backdrop to the festivities."Weather at that time was beautiful. Blue skies and all, which you hardly see now. Yeah, it was lovely," she said.Sonia also recalled that festivals were marked by Kashmiri cuisine and a traditional sweet rice preparation, a culinary tradition that continues in the family."And then, on festivals, we always used to have Kashmiri food and that sweet rice, like that, which we still make, by the way," she said.Sonia Gandhi has also documented several personal experiences and significant moments from her life in her memoir, titled *Belonging: A Journey of Love*. The book is scheduled to be launched on November 10.The memoir chronicles Sonia Gandhi's journey, from her childhood in post-war Italy and her romance that brought her to India to the personal losses that profoundly shaped her life and her relationship with her adopted country.In the book, the 79-year-old Congress veteran, who holds the distinction of being the party's longest-serving president, revisits her childhood in Italy, her relationship with Rajiv Gandhi during their time at Cambridge, and the assassinations of her mother-in-law, former prime minister Indira Gandhi, and her husband, Rajiv Gandhi.Get the latest India News and Live updates. articles.title: Pope Leo heads to Milei's Argentina:  Austerity, poverty and Iran war in focus
articles.summary: Pope Leo will arrive in Argentina on Sunday for the second leg of his 12-day South American tour, with his planned address and meeting with President
articles.body: Pope Leo will arrive in Argentina on Sunday for the second leg of his 12-day South American tour, with his planned address and meeting with President Javier Milei drawing attention amid differences between the Vatican and the Argentine government.The first US-born pope is expected to speak about issues including poverty, economic policy and political divisions. His remarks will be closely watched for possible indirect criticism of Milei, a libertarian leader and close ally of US President Donald Trump, Reuters reported.The Vatican has criticised aspects of Milei's austerity programme, saying spending cuts have hit the poorest sections of society hardest. Milei has also strongly supported the Iran war, which Leo has criticised, drawing Trump's ire.Leo is visiting Argentina after travelling to Uruguay, where he called on South American countries to work together on regional challenges and show how patient diplomacy can offer an alternative to conflict. His three-country tour will continue until November 17.The 71-year-old pontiff's visit is among the most closely watched foreign trips by a Catholic leader in recent decades. He is also the first pope to visit Argentina since 1987. During his stay until Wednesday, he is scheduled to visit four cities, Reuters reported.Why is Pope Leo's Argentina visit significant?Leo usually uses careful diplomatic language when addressing national governments during foreign visits. However, he has recently become a more outspoken voice on global issues, criticising the direction of world leadership.He is not expected to name Milei directly. However, any remarks on poverty, economic policy or political rhetoric could be interpreted as a response to the Argentine government's policies."Any interventions by Leo, particularly on poverty, the limits of markets or confrontational political rhetoric, could be read as implicit criticism of Milei and amplify existing opposition to the government's approach," Nicolas Watson, managing director at advisory firm Teneo, told Reuters.Milei came to power in 2023 after years of centre-left Peronist rule. During his campaign, he famously carried a chainsaw to symbolise his pledge to make deep cuts in government spending and put the country's finances in order.He has defended the austerity measures as necessary to control inflation. Annual inflation has fallen from more than 200% to 33% under his economic programme.However, surveys indicate that his popularity has declined ahead of elections next year. Argentines continue to face the effects of subsidy cuts, public-sector job losses and business closures, which have put pressure on household budgets.Leo's visit is expected to draw attention to people affected by economic hardship and social exclusion. His itinerary also includes visits to a care centre for people with disabilities and a prison.During his 18 months as pope, Leo has spoken out on the risks of artificial intelligence, urged world leaders to treat migrants more humanely and called for stronger action on climate change. These positions have put him at odds with Trump and other right-wing leaders.You use AI every day. Now get your AI Quotient. Take the AIQ test.

articles.title: Chicago’s 1893 World’s Fair introduced an unusual attraction, a two-speed moving sidewalk that carried visitors from the steamship pier to the Peristyle at 3 mph or 6 mph for five cents
articles.summary: The first moving walkway appeared in 1893 at the World’s Columbian Exposition in Chicago, United States.
articles.body: The first moving walkway appeared in 1893 at the World’s Columbian Exposition in Chicago, United States. It was also the longest ever, and riders paid five cents to use it. Separate levels let riders stand or sit while moving along the route. It ran over 1 kilometre along a pier and onwards to the Exposition entrance. According to John J. Flinn’s 1893 Official Guide to the World’s Columbian Exposition, one half of the platform travelled at three miles an hour, while the other moved at six miles an hour. Passengers paid five cents to use it at the exposition. The walkway was destroyed by fire in 1894, according to Guinness World Records.How the moving sidewalk worked at the 1893 World's FairThe guide lists the attraction under the heading ‘Moveable Sidewalk’ in its section of practical information for visitors. It calls it ‘a mechanical contrivance’ that carried passengers from the steamship landing at the pier to the Peristyle. The structure consisted of a continuous double platform. One half moved at three miles an hour and the other at six miles an hour.This arrangement gave passengers a choice of two moving speeds while travelling along the same route. The guide records a fare of five cents. It does not explain how passengers transferred between the two sections, how long the journey took, or how the machinery was powered.The walkway connected the pier with the PeristyleThe moving platform served as a route between the pier and the Peristyle, which stood at the water-facing entrance to the fair. The guide notes that boats from the city landed at the pier, which extended beyond the Peristyle. It also records that twenty turnstiles for the sale of admission tickets were located there.The walkway therefore connected the steamship landing with the area where visitors entered the exposition grounds. It identifies the starting point, destination, operating speeds, and fare. It gives no estimate of the platform’s overall length or passenger capacity.How visitors travelled across the exposition groundsThe walkway was one of several ways to move around the exposition grounds. The guide also describes the Intramural Railway, which ran around the outside of the grounds from the South Pond to the North Inlet. It provided a rapid means of travel, with stations at several points and a fare of ten cents for any distance. Trains travelled at about twelve miles an hour, and a complete circuit of the grounds took twenty minutes.Visitors could also hire rolling chairs at stations inside the main gates, near major buildings and at other points. articles.title: Australia planned to sell 67 military sites to raise $1.8 billion, but public protests over Sydney's 166-year-old Victoria Barracks prompted a November 8 reversal that will keep four historic sites publicly owned
articles.summary: The Australian government has dropped plans to sell several historic military sites, including the 166-year-old Victoria Barracks in Sydney.
articles.body: The Australian government has dropped plans to sell several historic military sites, including the 166-year-old Victoria Barracks in Sydney. The decision follows strong public opposition and concerns about protecting the country's military history. Prime Minister Anthony Albanese and Deputy Prime Minister Richard Marles announced the change on Sunday, 8 November 2026. They confirmed that Victoria Barracks in Sydney and three other important heritage sites will remain in public hands. The decision is a major change to the government's wider plan to sell military land that is no longer being used. The plan followed an independent review of Defence properties, which recommended selling or partly selling 67 sites. The sales were expected to raise between $1.8 billion and $3 billion for military upgrades. Under the revised plan, four important historic sites will remain publicly owned. The government will now look at other public, heritage and commercial uses for the properties.Heritage sites spared from private saleThe main site affected by the decision is Victoria Barracks in Paddington, Sydney. The historic sandstone complex was built between 1841 and 1848 and is considered one of Australia's finest examples of British military architecture. "Victoria Barracks Sydney has a special place in our nation's history, and we will be keeping it in public hands," Albanese said in an official statement released by the Prime Minister's office. Along with the Sydney site, the government confirmed that Victoria Barracks in Melbourne, Fort Queenscliff in Victoria and RAAF Williams at Point Cook in Victoria will also remain publicly owned. Instead of selling these properties to private developers, the government plans to work with the Australian War Memorial to record and share their history. Large parts of the military sites, which were previously closed to the public, are expected to become accessible to visitors. "Most Sydneysiders have not availed themselves of the opportunity to see the history that has been made here over such a long period of time," Albanese told reporters while discussing the review of Defence properties.Strategic refocusing and Indigenous land returnsAlthough the four major heritage sites will remain in public hands, the wider sale programme will continue. Dozens of other military properties are still being considered for sale or transfer. The aim is to reduce Defence costs and free up money for new military equipment. Defence minister Richard Marles said the cost of maintaining land that is no longer needed takes money away from important military operations. "Given the strategic landscape we face, we cannot afford to be wasting money," Marles said in a joint statement. "Every person who wears our nation's uniform matters. Every hour they spend in it counts, and every dollar which resources them is precious."As part of the first stage of the plan, some properties will be transferred to local communities or Indigenous groups. The government confirmed that part of the Stokes Hill Fuel Installation in the Northern Territory will be returned to its Traditional Owners, the Larrakia people. The area includes land registered as sacred under Northern Territory law. Other sites, including Kowandi North in Darwin, will be considered for future uses that support housing and community needs. The government has also outlined plans for the remaining parts of HMAS Penguin in New South Wales, where the Angophora Forest will be transferred to the Sydney Harbour Federation Trust.You use AI every day. articles.title: A North Dakota grandmother and her longtime partner cared for her grandson from the age of four months, and both parents consented to adoption; the state Supreme Court says the unmarried couple cannot adopt jointly
articles.summary: Unmarried couples cannot legally adopt a child together under North Dakota law, the state's Supreme Court has ruled.
articles.body: Unmarried couples cannot legally adopt a child together under North Dakota law, the state's Supreme Court has ruled. The decision blocks a joint adoption request by a grandmother and her partner, who have cared for her grandson since he was four months old. The ruling was issued on Friday, 6 November 2026. It answered a legal question sent to the Supreme Court by the McKenzie County District Court about the state's adoption laws. The case involved an unmarried couple, identified in court records as D.W. and A.D., who have lived together since 2007. A.D. is the child's maternal grandmother. The boy, identified as T.J.W.-H., was left in her care by his mother when he was four months old. Both of his biological parents later signed documents agreeing to give up their parental rights and allow the adoption to take place. Although both parents had agreed to the adoption and the child lived with the couple until he was three years old, the state's highest court ruled that North Dakota law does not allow two unmarried adults to adopt a child together.Strict reading of statutory categoriesWriting the decision for a unanimous court, Justice Douglas Bahr explained that state law sets clear rules about who can apply to adopt a child. Under Section 14-15-03 of the North Dakota Century Code, lawmakers have listed specific groups of people who can adopt a child. The law allows a husband and wife to adopt together, a step-parent to adopt their spouse's child, or "an unmarried adult" to adopt a child alone. The court ruled that the words "an unmarried adult" refer to one person adopting alone. They do not allow two unmarried adults to apply as a couple. "The absence of the word 'together' and of any limit on when and how many unmarried adults may adopt supports the conclusion the legislature intended section 14-15-03(2) to apply to one unmarried adult, not to two or more unmarried adults," Justice Bahr wrote. The court also pointed out that North Dakota's adoption laws were based on the 1969 Uniform Adoption Act. That law allowed married couples to apply for joint adoptions but did not give the same right to unmarried couples.Policy choices rest with lawmakersThe Supreme Court said that deciding who is allowed to adopt a child is the responsibility of lawmakers, not judges. "The legislature, not the judiciary, determines the public policy of who is eligible to adopt," the court stated in its ruling. The decision also referred to earlier court cases in other US states with similar adoption laws. These included appeals court decisions in Maine, Louisiana and Wisconsin, which also rejected joint adoption requests from unmarried couples living together. The justices noted that some states, including Wyoming, have changed their laws to allow unmarried partners to adopt children together. However, North Dakota lawmakers have not made a similar change. The court said judges cannot extend joint adoption rights to unmarried couples simply because they live together. Such a change would require a clear amendment to the law by the North Dakota Legislative Assembly.Implications for the McKenzie County petitionThe legal question sent to the Supreme Court asked: "Is an unmarried couple able to adopt a child pursuant to any provision of N.D.C.C. § 14-15-03?" By answering "no", the Supreme Court has effectively stopped D.W. and A.D. from becoming the child's joint legal parents through their shared adoption application. However, the ruling does not prevent either person from applying to adopt the child individually. Under the current law, one of them could submit an application as a single unmarried adult. If approved, only that person would receive legal parental rights through the adoption. Chief Justice Lisa Fair McEvers and Justices Jerod E. Tufte and Jon J. Jensen fully agreed with the decision. The case has now been sent back to the McKenzie County District Court, which will continue handling the adoption matter in line with the Supreme Court's ruling.You use AI every day. articles.title: ‘Not a political book, but a personal one’: Sonia Gandhi ahead of memoir release
articles.summary: NEW DELHI: Two days before the India release of her memoir, Congress leader Sonia Gandhi on Sunday described it as “not a political book but a personal
articles.body: NEW DELHI: Two days before the India release of her memoir, Congress leader Sonia Gandhi on Sunday described it as “not a political book but a personal one," emphasising that she wanted to portray her family "honestly," as people she knew and loved.“This is not a political book, it’s a personal one. Much has been written about my family, but rarely with real insight into who they were, their motivations, their struggles, their very human flaws. I wanted to portray them honestly, as people I knew and loved,” the Congress Parliamentary Party chairperson wrote on X.She gave a detailed account of how the book, titled "Belonging: A Journey of Love," came to be, in an article for The Hindu, which had published a detailed interview with her on Saturday."For most of my life, I kept my inner world to myself. Even after grief pulled me into politics, I held on to whatever privacy I could, and writing openly about my life felt almost unthinkable. Only after stepping back from the daily churn of public life could I see my own story clearly," Sonia Gandhi wrote in the article, referring to the assassination of her husband, former Prime Minister Rajiv Gandhi, who was India's youngest Prime Minister.Also Read | Watch: Sonia, Priyanka take a trip down memory lane, recall Diwali with Rajiv Gandhi"When I did look back, one thread ran through all of it: love, and the loyalty that grows from it. It all began in England, where a 19-year-old woman from a small Italian town met a young Indian student (Rajiv Gandhi). It carried me into a new country and a new family, into a deep bond with my mother-in-law (Indira Gandhi), and through the years of raising our children," she added,"It also carried me through the unbearable, when I lost first my mother-in-law and then my husband to violence," the former Congress president wrote.Published by HarperCollins India, Sonia Gandhi's memoir will be released in India on November 10, ending uncertainty over the book's domestic publication following an "impasse" between the author's representatives and Penguin Random House India.The book covers major tragedies that impacted the Gandhi family, including the death of Sonia Gandhi's brother-in-law Sanjay Gandhi in a plane crash, Indira Gandhi's assassination in 1984 and Rajiv Gandhi's assassination in 1991.The memoir also delves into political events surrounding the Congress' victory in the 2004 elections, when Sonia Gandhi declined to become Prime Minister and instead led the party and its alliance, which governed India till 2014.Get the latest India News and Live updates. articles.title: ‘Threatened to kill him’: Jaipur cafe owner ambushed, beaten after objecting to employee's friend's frequent visits- video
articles.summary: JAIPUR: A cafe owner was brutally attacked by unidentified assailants in the Vaishali Nagar area of Jaipur late on November 5.
articles.body: JAIPUR: A cafe owner was brutally attacked by unidentified assailants in the Vaishali Nagar area of Jaipur late on November 5.The attackers, who arrived on motorcycles and scooters, allegedly ambushed him as he was walking home after closing his cafe. They repeatedly assaulted him with sticks, leaving him critically injured before fleeing the spot.A video of the incident surfaced on Sunday. Police have registered an FIR based on a complaint filed by the victim’s family and are searching for the attackers with the help of CCTV footage.Police suspect the involvement of a friend of a woman employee who works at the cafe. The man reportedly visited the cafe frequently, which the owner had objected to. Following this, the woman’s friend allegedly threatened to kill the cafe owner.SHO (Vaishali Nagar) Arvind Singh Shekhawat said that Mayank Gopalia (34), a resident of Vaishali Nagar, was attacked. He runs Oven The Bakery Cafe on Vaishali Marg.On November 5, at around 9.45 pm, Mayank was walking home after closing his cafe when the assailants, who were waiting a short distance away, approached him from behind and attacked him with sticks.After being hit on the head, Mayank fell to the ground. The attackers continued beating him. Believing him to be dead, they fled the spot along with their accomplices, who were waiting on motorcycles and scooters.Passers-by spotted Mayank lying in a pool of blood and rushed him to hospital. Due to the severity of his injuries, he had to undergo surgery on his head.After receiving information, Vaishali Nagar police reached the hospital and gathered details about the attackers from Mayank’s family members and cafe employees, as he was unconscious.An examination of CCTV footage from the area revealed that the attackers, who had arrived on motorcycles and scooters, were waiting near a turn in the lane. As soon as Mayank entered the lane, they attacked him with sticks, leaving him critically injured before fleeing.A preliminary police investigation revealed that Mayank had an altercation with a female employee at the cafe on the afternoon of November 5. A friend of the woman reportedly visited her frequently at the cafe. On the day of the incident, Mayank objected to his visit. The man allegedly threatened to kill him before leaving.The SHO said Mayank was not in a condition to record his statement until Saturday night. articles.title: Queen Elizabeth II’s final days at Balmoral Castle: Inside the 53,000-acre Scottish estate where she found peace, made cherished family memories and spent her last moments surrounded by nature and loved ones
articles.summary: Queen Elizabeth II spent the final days of her life at Balmoral Castle in Scotland, a place that held a special place in her heart and was associated with
articles.body: Queen Elizabeth II spent the final days of her life at Balmoral Castle in Scotland, a place that held a special place in her heart and was associated with some of her happiest family memories. Located in the Scottish Highlands, the sprawling 53,000-acre royal estate served as a private summer retreat for generations of the British royal family. It was also where the longest-reigning British monarch breathed her last on September 8, 2022, having chosen to spend her final days at a place she deeply loved.Away from the demands of royal engagements and public appearances, Balmoral offered the Queen an opportunity to enjoy a quieter life. Every August, the royal family would retreat to the Scottish estate, spending time away from the public eye. Their days often involved entertaining friends, attending dances, fishing, picnicking in the countryside and going on shooting parties.Why Balmoral Castle was Queen Elizabeth's happiest placeQueen Elizabeth's affection for Balmoral was no secret. In the 2016 documentary ‘Our Queen at Ninety’, her granddaughter Princess Eugenie spoke about how much the monarch loved spending time at the Scottish estate.“I think Granny is the most happy there. I think she really, really loves the Highlands,” Princess Eugenie said.The late Sir Malcolm Ross, former Comptroller of the Royal Household, also spoke about the peaceful surroundings that made Balmoral so special to the Queen. In an interview with the BBC, he said, “It’s the wide open spaces. No distractions, no aeroplanes, no noise, no traffic. Just this lovely estate where she can freely roam everywhere.”He further explained that the estate allowed the monarch to relax with her dogs and enjoy the simple pleasures of life. “She can relax, with her dogs, just doing what she thought normal people did, and indeed what normal people do,” he said.Balmoral Castle has been a royal retreat for over 170 yearsBalmoral has served as a summer retreat for the British royal family for more than 170 years. The estate was purchased by Prince Albert, Queen Victoria's husband, in 1852. Initially spanning around 17,000 acres, the property has since expanded to more than 53,000 acres.According to the castle and estate's official website, Balmoral encompasses vast stretches of moorland and heath, towering hills and rare, protected woodland habitats. The property also includes the immediate surroundings of the castle, with landscaped lawns, gardens, native plant species, mazes and a nine-hole golf course.For Queen Elizabeth, the estate was much more than a royal residence. She enjoyed spending time outdoors, riding horses and walking her dogs across the expansive grounds. Speaking about the freedom the Scottish Highlands offered, she once said, as quoted on Balmoral's website, “You can go out for miles and never see anybody; there are endless possibilities.”The time Queen Elizabeth met American tourists at BalmoralThe Queen's relaxed approach to life at Balmoral was also reflected in her interactions with visitors. Former royal protection officer Richard Griffin, popularly known as Dick, once recalled an amusing encounter with two American tourists during a walk around the estate.According to Reuters, one of the tourists recognised that the elderly woman walking alongside Griffin bore a striking resemblance to Queen Elizabeth. The tourist then asked the monarch whether she had ever met the Queen.Griffin recalled that the monarch responded instantly with a sense of humour, saying, “I haven’t, but Dick here meets her regularly.”The tourists subsequently asked for a photograph, and Queen Elizabeth happily obliged by taking a picture of them with Griffin. The incident offered a glimpse into the monarch's playful side and her ability to enjoy ordinary moments away from royal protocol.Queen Elizabeth continued her royal duties during her stay at BalmoralAlthough Balmoral allowed Queen Elizabeth to enjoy a more relaxed lifestyle, her time at the estate was not entirely free of official responsibilities. She continued to carry out her royal duties, reading diplomatic papers that were delivered to her daily in the familiar red boxes.The Queen also welcomed foreign dignitaries and British politicians to the Scottish Highlands. The British prime minister traditionally visited her at Balmoral once a year, making the estate an important setting for official meetings despite its reputation as a private family retreat.King Charles reveals why his mother chose Balmoral for her final daysQueen Elizabeth's emotional connection with Balmoral remained strong until the end of her life. In a speech to the Scottish Parliament in 2024, King Charles spoke about his mother's attachment to the estate and revealed that she had chosen to spend her final days there.“My late mother especially treasured the time spent at Balmoral, and it was there, in the most beloved of places, where she chose to spend her final days,” the King said.However, Princess Anne later revealed that the Queen had once expressed concerns about the possibility of dying at Balmoral, as it could complicate arrangements following her death.In the documentary ‘Charles III: The Coronation Year’, Princess Anne recalled, “I think there was a moment when she felt it would be more difficult if she died at Balmoral. I think we did try to persuade her that that shouldn’t be part of the decision-making process. So I hope she felt that was right in the end, because we did.”Queen Elizabeth eventually breathed her last at Balmoral on September 8, 2022, bringing to a close a remarkable chapter in British royal history at a place that had been particularly close to her heart.Can the public visit Balmoral Castle?Balmoral is now the private property of King Charles, and the royal family continues to spend part of the late summer at the Scottish estate. However, the property also welcomes members of the public during designated periods of the year.Visitors can explore parts of the grounds, stroll through the gardens, view exhibitions and enjoy the surrounding countryside. The estate also offers holiday cottages for those looking to experience a stay in the Scottish Highlands.For Queen Elizabeth, Balmoral was never just another royal residence. It was a place where she could step away from the responsibilities of the Crown, spend time with her family, enjoy nature and experience the simple pleasures of life. It was fitting that the monarch chose to spend her final days at the Scottish retreat that had brought her so much happiness throughout her life.You use AI every day. Now get your AI Quotient. articles.title: A Renaissance landscape acquired by a Swiss collector’s father in 1957 vanished from public view for nearly 70 years; experts have identified it as a rare Altdorfer worth up to £5 million
articles.summary: A painting that remained in a private collection and out of public view for nearly seven decades is now attracting attention from the international art
articles.body: A painting that remained in a private collection and out of public view for nearly seven decades is now attracting attention from the international art world. Created around 1520 by German Renaissance artist Albrecht Altdorfer, the small landscape depicts a densely wooded forest, a rainbow behind the trees and a distant castle beneath a cloudy sky. The artwork was acquired by a Swiss collector's father in 1957 and remained out of public view until its recent identification as a rare work by the Renaissance master.The painting, titled A Thickly Wooded Landscape With a Rainbow Behind the Trees and a Distant Outcrop to the Right Beneath a Cloud-Laden Sky, will be offered at Sotheby's Old Masters Evening Sale in London on December 9, 2026. According to Sotheby's auction catalogue, the work carries an estimated value of £3 million to £5 million. Its rediscovery is particularly important because it is only the third known oil landscape by Altdorfer, making it a significant addition to the known works of one of the Northern Renaissance's leading artists.A painting kept in a private collection since 1957The artwork has an unusual history. Before reaching its present owner, it belonged to the collection of the Austrian noble House of Harrach in Vienna. The current owner's father acquired it from the collection in 1957, and it subsequently remained in the family. The present owner inherited the painting, which had remained outside public view for approximately 70 years.The work was previously unknown to Altdorfer scholars and was not included in the artist's catalogue raisonné, a detailed scholarly record of an artist's known works. Its identification earlier this year has therefore expanded the recognised body of paintings attributed to the German master. The painting is relatively small, measuring 23.4 by 19.8 centimetres. It is signed with Altdorfer's monogram, AA, on the trunk of a larch tree. Sotheby's catalogue describes the medium as oil on parchment, which was later attached to a wooden panel, probably made of limewood.What makes the landscape special?The painting's subject is a thick forest under a cloud-filled sky, with a rainbow visible behind the trees and a distant rocky outcrop supporting a castle. Despite its small dimensions, the artwork creates a detailed natural scene through its treatment of trees, light, clouds and the surrounding landscape.According to The Art Newspaper, George Gordon, chairman of Sotheby’s Worldwide Old Masters Department, described the painting’s rediscovery as “one of the most exciting discoveries imaginable in our field”, as it adds to the known body of work of one of the great masters of the Northern Renaissance.Its rarity also contributes to its importance. Before this painting was identified, only two other pure oil landscapes by Altdorfer were known. One, Landscape With a Footbridge, is held by the National Gallery in London, while Landscape of the Danube near Regensburg is part of the Alte Pinakothek collection in Munich. Both are in museums, making the newly identified work an exceptionally rare opportunity for collectors.Who was Albrecht Altdorfer?Albrecht Altdorfer was an important German Renaissance artist associated with Regensburg, Bavaria, known for his paintings, drawings and engravings. He is regarded as one of the pioneers of independent landscape painting in Europe, particularly for giving natural scenery a central place in art rather than treating it merely as a background for religious or historical subjects.Altdorfer began producing landscape drawings around 1511, including scenes inspired by the natural surroundings along the Danube. He later became known for detailed depictions of forests and landscapes near Regensburg. His paintings often featured dense vegetation, dramatic skies and expressive natural forms.Altdorfer also received important royal commissions. One of his best-known works, The Battle of Alexander at Issus, was painted in 1529 for Duke Wilhelm IV of Bavaria and is now housed in the Alte Pinakothek in Munich. He served Emperor Maximilian I from 1513 and later returned to Regensburg, where he died in 1538.Why the upcoming auction is significantThe December sale will mark the first time a known Altdorfer painting has appeared on the market since 1980. At that time, the National Gallery privately acquired his Christ Taking Leave of His Mother, painted around 1520, for a reported £2.4 million. Sotheby's has estimated the newly identified landscape at £3 million to £5 million, although Gordon has indicated that it could potentially sell for more. He also expects museums to show interest in the work because of its rarity and historical significance.Before the auction, the painting is scheduled to be exhibited at Sotheby's in New York from November 7 to 19, followed by a London exhibition from December 4 to 9. Its appearance gives art enthusiasts and potential buyers an opportunity to see a Renaissance landscape that remained outside public view for generations.The rediscovery is more than an auction story. It brings a previously unrecognised work into the documented history of a major Renaissance artist and offers a rare glimpse into his approach to landscape painting nearly five centuries ago.You use AI every day. articles.title: What we know so far after Krakow gun attack
articles.summary: Six people were killed in a random shooting in Krakow's main square, and three bodies were later found at the home of the attacker.
articles.body:
At least six people were killed and more than a dozen others injured when a gunman suspected to have ties to the far-right opened fire in central Krakow, the second largest city in Poland.

Three bodies were found at his home when it was searched by police. Here is everything we know so far.

The attack began shortly before 15:00 local time (14:00 GMT) in Krakow's Main Market Square, the bustling central point of the city which is popular with tourists.

Police said a man drove into the square before beginning to fire "at random people from his car".

Footage shows scenes of panic as people fled, with the sound of gunfire clearly heard.

A passing tram was shot at during the apparently random attack, shattering windows but no passengers were injured.

Armed officers raced to the scene and engaged in a gunfight with the suspect, who was shot within three minutes of the attack beginning, preventing a further massacre, officials said.

A 25-year-old man who was arrested remains in hospital after having surgery for a gunshot wound. The Krakow branch of the National Public Prosecutor's Office in Poland has announced an investigation into what constitutes "a terrorist offence".

Distressing footage authenticated by BBC Verify shows the moment a police officer confronts the suspect on the ground before firing his weapon several times.

The officer then falls to the ground, apparently having been injured himself.

Shop windows in the square have signs of damage, seemingly from bullets, with glass shards scattered along the floor.

City officials have urged people who live in the city and tourists to stay away from the area while an investigation continues.

The suspect's car, found at the intersection of Dietla and Stradomska streets, was checked for possible explosive devices, police said, but none were found. Residents of nearby buildings had been evacuated while the operation was under way.

How many people have died and been injured?

Six people - four women and two men - are confirmed to have been killed in central Krakow. Four victims are Polish, while a British national and an Austrian woman were also killed.

Poland's Prime Minister Donald Tusk said three bodies - two women and one man - were found at the gunman's house when it was searched after the attack.

On Sunday, Polish police confirmed those three victims had been identified as the alleged gunman's 53-year-old father, 52-year-old mother and his sister, who was 21-years-old.

Sixteen people, including five foreigners, two police officers and the attacker, were taken to hospital. The interior ministry later said they were from Austria, Britain, Germany, Portugal and Russia.

Tusk later named the injured officers as Senior Constable Jakub Kulik and Senior Constable Artur Morański.

One of the police officers was described as being in a "very critical condition" by a Polish government minister after being shot three times while arresting the attacker. The officer is undergoing surgery, he added.

In an update on Sunday, police spokesperson Katarzyna Cislo told Radio Krakow two women who were sent to hospital following the incident had been released and the remaining individuals in Krakow's hospitals are in a stable condition.

She said this included the two police officers who were injured.

Polish authorities have not confirmed the names and ages of the other victims.

What do we know about the suspect and motive?

Police have identified the attacker as a 25-year-old Polish man but have not confirmed his name.

Local governor Krzysztof Jan Klęczar said the gunman remains in a critical condition at hospital.

The suspect was wearing "military-style attire" and had a military-grade weapon, according to a police spokesperson. However, authorities said he was not a soldier.

"Many pieces of weapons and ammunition were found in his vehicle", the spokesperson added.

Polish media has reported the suspect had a firearms permit and may have obtained the weapons from his family home.

A minister has said early investigations indicate he was inspired by "far-right ideologies". The minister also described him as an "ultra-nationalist" without giving further details.

His home in Ostrowiec Świętokrzyski, a city around 200km (125 miles) from Krakow, has been searched with support from counter-terrorism police.

The shooting happened in one of the largest medieval squares in Europe, a busy location which is also a popular tourist destination.

Jonathan Balshaw from Ipswich was there with his Polish girlfriend Dominika. The couple were outside St Mary's Basilica, in the corner of the square, when the shooting started.

Jonathan said: "We ran down the side of the church and through the side door and hid with several other people until the gunfire died down.

"A lot of shots were fired, more than 20 with it sounding like multiple different firearms - there were two distinctly different noises."

Caitlin Shasby from Newcastle arrived in Krakow yesterday with her friend Jon for a long weekend.

She said they heard shots from their hotel room but were not sure what was happening until their hotel rang them and told them to "stay in our rooms until further notice".

Local media outlet Gazeta Krakowska reported two surgeons rushed to help after the shooting stopped.

Dr Mateusz Wierdak and Prof Michał Pędziwiatr spoke to the media outlet saying they helped the wounded after having lunch with their families.

Pędziwiatr says two police officers "were conscious, in superficial contact with gunshot wounds to the chest", adding: "The perpetrator was also conscious, expressed pain, and had gunshot wounds to the abdomen, thigh, and chest."

"We don't feel like heroes, but we did everything a paramedic would do at the scene of such an incident."

What has the reaction been in Poland and internationally?

After travelling to Krakow, Prime Minister Donald Tusk said : "Until now in Poland we haven't had such drastic cases of terrorism...that's what we have to call this cruel attack on people's lives here in Krakow."

Krakow Mayor Łukasz Gibała has signed an order declaring a period of mourning in the city which will last until Wednesday, 11 November.

UK Prime Minister Andy Burnham said: "I'm shocked and saddened by the appalling shooting in Kraków today."

"My thoughts are with the families of those who have lost their lives, everyone injured and all those affected by this senseless violence. The United Kingdom stands in solidarity with the people of Poland," he added.

British foreign secretary Ed Miliband said on social media the UK government "deeply mourns" those who died in the "appalling attack".

US ambassador to Poland Tom Rose described it as a "savage and murderous attack".

The EU's top diplomat, Kaja Kallas, said the shooting was "a tragedy that will be felt far beyond Poland".

President Volodymyr Zelensky of neighbouring Ukraine called the shooting "shocking."

"On behalf of the Ukrainian people, and personally, I extend my sincere condolences to the families and loved ones of the victims," he wrote on social media.

articles.body: Parents of a nine-year-old British Hindu boy have approached the UK high court after his primary school in London allegedly stopped him from wearing a tilak on his forehead, news agency PTI reported on Sunday.The boy, who belongs to the Swaminarayan faith tradition, had been studying at Vicar's Green Primary School in west London since 2021. He had worn the sacred religious marking, known as Tilak-Chandlo, to school for several years without any objection.However, the school raised concerns over the practice in late 2025, triggering a dispute that eventually led his parents to withdraw him from the institution and initiate legal proceedings.“As parents, it has been heartbreaking to see our son go through this simply because he wanted to practise his faith,” the parents said in a statement released by their legal team this weekend.“He had worn his Tilak-Chandlo to school for years without difficulty, and we never imagined that something so sacred to our family would become a source of distress,” they said.“Our son was just an ordinary little boy who enjoyed learning and spending time with his friends. His religious marking did not hurt anyone or prevent him from being a good pupil.“We have always taught our children to respect every religion, and we simply ask that the same respect be shown to ours. We hope that no other child will have to choose between their education and their faith,” they added.The family has filed a case in the High Court of England and Wales, seeking £25,000 in damages. The proceedings are ongoing, and the allegations remain disputed.“This case goes beyond one child or one school. It raises important questions about religious freedom and equality in British education,” the lawyer representing the child said.“No child should feel compelled to choose between their faith and their education. We hope these proceedings will help clarify the rights of children from all religious backgrounds,” he added.The family has also alleged that after the school objected to the religious marking, staff repeatedly questioned the boy about his religious practices and restricted his participation in certain school activities.The school, however, has denied allegations of discrimination, saying it acted sensitively, recognised the family's religious beliefs and offered alternative arrangements that the parents chose not to accept.Vicar's Green Primary School has maintained that it values and respects the diverse cultural and religious backgrounds of its community. It said its policy was designed to “promote cohesion, fairness, equality and a shared sense of belonging while preventing division or disruption within the school community”.The family's legal challenge is being supported by interfaith initiative Action for Harmony.You use AI every day. articles.title: PM Modi visits LK Advani on his birthday as veteran BJP leader enters 100th year
articles.summary: NEW DELHI: Prime Minister Narendra Modi on Sunday visited former deputy prime minister Lal Krishna Advani at his residence to greet him on his birthday,
articles.body: NEW DELHI: Prime Minister Narendra Modi on Sunday visited former deputy prime minister Lal Krishna Advani at his residence to greet him on his birthday, as the veteran BJP leader entered his 100th year.The Bharatiya Janata Party also organised a havan at its headquarters to mark the occasion. Senior party leaders, including BJP national president Nitin Nabin, attended the ceremony, held between 10am and 10.30am.PM Modi marked the occasion by writing an article on Advani's contribution to Indian politics and the BJP. In a post on X, the prime minister said he had recalled Advani's journey, from experiencing the Partition and rebuilding his life to strengthening the Jana Sangh, building the BJP and standing up to the Emergency.He also referred to Advani's role in the Somnath-Ayodhya Rath Yatra and his time in government, besides highlighting his interests in reading, culture, cinema and writing.PM Modi also credited Advani's leadership with expanding the BJP's political presence."Today, 8th November, is a landmark day. Respected L.K. Advani Ji enters his hundredth year. On this special occasion, my greetings to him. I’ve written an article in which I’ve highlighted his everlasting contribution to India," he said."I have recalled his journey, be it experiencing the horrors of Partition and rebuilding life from scratch, strengthening the Jana Sangh and building the BJP, standing up for democracy during the Emergency, leading the Somnath to Ayodhya Rath Yatra or serving the nation in government. Have also written about other aspects of Advani Ji - the voracious reader, his love for culture and cinema, a prolific writer and more," he added.Nabin also extended birthday wishes to Advani, describing him as a guide to party workers and acknowledging his contribution to the organisation's growth and the Ram Janmabhoomi movement.Born on November 8, 1927, in Karachi, in present-day Pakistan, Advani joined the RSS in 1942. He served as BJP president for three terms between 1986 and 2005 and was India's deputy prime minister from 2002 to 2004. He was awarded the Bharat Ratna in 2024.Get the latest India News and Live updates. Download the TOI app.

articles.title: Gadi Eisenkot officially gets first chance to form Israel’s next government
articles.summary: Israeli opposition leader and former army chief Gadi Eisenkot was on Sunday formally tasked by President Isaac Herzog with forming the country's next
articles.body: Israeli opposition leader and former army chief Gadi Eisenkot was on Sunday formally tasked by President Isaac Herzog with forming the country's next government after the October 27 parliamentary elections resulted in a fractured mandate.This came a day after Herzog designated Eisenkot, the main challenger to outgoing Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu, to form the next government.With the mandate now formally in his hands, the Yashar party leader will begin complicated negotiations with potential coalition partners. He will have up to six weeks to form a government.Speaking after formally receiving the mandate, Eisenkot laid out several “preconditions” for parties seeking to join his potential government."The conditions are support for Israel as a Jewish and democratic state, for its declaration of independence, for military or national service, and recognising Hamas as a terrorist organisation," The Associated Press quoted him as saying."I want a leadership that people can trust, that will act in the interests of the public and that represents all parts of society," he added.Also Read: Is Netanyahu's time up? 10 things to know as rival Gadi Eisenkot gets shot at power in IsraelNeither Netanyahu nor Eisenkot secured a majority in the election. The Netanyahu-led coalition saw its strength fall from a peak of 68 seats in the 120-member Knesset to just 53. The opposition bloc, led by Eisenkot, won 48 seats, while Arab-led parties secured the remaining 19.However, following consultations last week, Herzog concluded that the former army chief had the strongest chance of forming a coalition, as Arab-led parties had expressed their willingness to support him.You use AI every day. articles.body: Ahmedabad: Bathroom fittings and accessories worth Rs 8.6 lakh were stolen from the office of a residential project coming up in Bhadaj between Friday evening and Saturday morning.According to a complaint filed with Sola police on Saturday night, the complainant, a 28-year-old sales executive working at Alabhya Construction site, said he and his employer had locked the site office around 6pm on Friday before leaving.When he returned around 11am on Saturday, he found a sliding window open and office materials scattered. articles.title: New Zealand faces political uncertainty as special votes could reshape election result
articles.summary: New Zealand faces weeks of political uncertainty after a closely fought general election left prime minister Christopher Luxon’s centre-right National-led
articles.body: New Zealand faces weeks of political uncertainty after a closely fought general election left prime minister Christopher Luxon’s centre-right National-led coalition with only a wafer-thin majority in preliminary results, while nearly 400,000 special votes remain to be counted.The National Party, along with its coalition partners ACT and New Zealand First, is projected to win 67 seats in a 131-member Parliament, just one more than the 66 required for a majority. However, the final outcome could change when special votes, including ballots cast overseas and outside voters’ electorates, are counted.The Electoral Commission is expected to announce the official results on November 27. Until then, Luxon’s government will continue in a caretaker capacity, with coalition negotiations likely to follow the final count.Neither Luxon nor opposition leader Chris Hipkins claimed victory after Saturday’s election. Luxon said the contest was “too close to call”, but maintained that National had a “pathway” to forming the next government.“National is once again the largest party in Parliament, and we have a pathway to forming the next government,” he told supporters in Auckland, adding that negotiations and compromises would be necessary.Hipkins, whose Labour Party is projected to win 36 seats, also stopped short of conceding. “New Zealand has spoken. It may take us a little bit longer to figure out exactly what it is that you’ve said,” he told supporters, insisting that every vote must be counted.National has secured 42 seats, while Labour is followed by the Greens with 16, ACT with 13, New Zealand First with 12, the centrist Opportunity Party with seven and Te Pāti Māori with five, according to preliminary projections.The close contest has made the smaller parties crucial to government formation. Opportunity, led by Qiulae Wong, has crossed the 5% threshold required to enter Parliament, marking the first time a new party without roots in established political groups has cleared the threshold since New Zealand adopted its mixed-member proportional (MMP) system in 1996.Wong has said her party is open to working with either side, but would first negotiate with the party that wins the most seats. Luxon, who had previously ruled out working with Opportunity, struck a more conciliatory tone after the results, saying he wanted to build a relationship with Wong and find common ground.The party could become a kingmaker if the National-led bloc loses its narrow majority after the special votes are counted. The opposition grouping of Labour, the Greens and Te Pāti Māori is projected to have 57 seats, and would also need Opportunity’s support to form a government.Special votes could prove decisive. They have historically tended to favour the left: in the 2023 election, they helped Te Pāti Māori and the Greens gain three seats between them. The final count could therefore alter the balance of power, particularly given the narrow margins in several electorates.New Zealand’s MMP system gives voters two choices, one for their local electorate representative and another for a political party. The party vote determines each party’s proportional share of seats, while parties that win more electorate seats than their share of the party vote allows can retain the additional seats, creating what is known as an “overhang”.The election campaign was dominated by the cost of living, unemployment and concerns over the sluggish economy. High grocery and fuel prices, along with healthcare, were among the issues that shaped voter choices.The results also point to declining support for the two parties that have traditionally dominated New Zealand politics. National and Labour have each secured around 29% of the popular vote, with smaller parties gaining ground across the political spectrum.The Treaty of Waitangi, New Zealand’s founding document, was another major campaign issue, particularly among Māori voters. The Treaty Principles Bill, which sought to define the Treaty’s principles in law, was defeated in 2025. Te Pāti Māori co-leader Debbie Ngarewa-Packer has indicated that her party could work with Labour, the Greens and Opportunity to remove the incumbent government.With the special votes still to be counted, the country could face weeks of negotiations before a new government takes shape. Political observers have also warned that the process may extend beyond the final results, potentially leaving New Zealand without a confirmed government.You use AI every day. articles.title: Maharashtra SIR: Only 17% of over 2 crore deletions due to deaths, finds study
articles.summary: Study: Maharashtra SIR cut 2.07 crore voters; only 17% due to deaths. MMR saw nearly 1 in 3 deleted, with urban areas driving non-death removals.
articles.body: Mumbai: The special intensive revision (SIR) of poll rolls has led to the deletion of nearly one in three electors in MMR, according to a preliminary independent study by Sabar Institute, a public policy research organisation.Thane recorded 28.6 lakh deletions, accounting for 38.4% of its pre-SIR electorate of 74.5 lakh. Mumbai city followed with 9.5 lakh deletions, 37.2% of 25.6 lakh voters. Mumbai suburban recorded 26.6 lakh deletions, 33.9% of its 78.3 lakh electorate.The study found that Mumbai’s 36 assembly constituencies accounted for 17% of Maharashtra’s total deletions despite having only 11% of its pre-revision electorate. The deletion rate in these constituencies was 34.7%, against 19.5% in the rest of the state.Across the state, 2.07 crore names were struck off. Only 16.8% of these were attributed to deaths, and 83% categorised as permanently shifted, untraceable or absent, or already enrolled elsewhere, the report said.Thane topped the state in non-death deletions at 35.4%, followed by Mumbai city at 31.6% and Mumbai suburban at 29.7%. Pune, Nagpur and Palghar recorded 28.1%, 25.9% and 25.1%, respectively.Non-death deletions exceeded the 2024 assembly election victory margin in 190 of Maharashtra’s 288 constituencies. In 95 constituencies, the untraceable/absent category alone exceeded the winning margin.The report suggested that urbanisation is a stronger indicator of deletion patterns than caste or religious compositions of districts.Colaba recorded nearly 1.2 lakh deletions—46.9% of its pre-revision electorate—making it the second highest proportion among the 288 constituencies. It is the only constituency in the state where deletions exceeded votes cast (1,18,499) in the 2024 assembly polls, found the study.Constituencies with lower turnout in the 2024 assembly election recorded higher non-death deletions, suggesting a relationship between lower electoral participation and older or less frequently updated voter rolls.The report found that women and men were removed at almost identical overall rates—21.4% and 21.2%, respectively. However, among voters aged 18-29 marked as permanently shifted outside Mumbai, 8.2 lakh were women compared with 3.8 lakh men. Researchers said this pattern was consistent with women moving into marital homes. In Mumbai, though, the pattern reversed, with 85,167 young men and 76,848 young women recorded among the deletions, which the study said was consistent with male-dominated labour migration.Third gender electors were disproportionately affected. As many as 3,250 (53.3%) of the 6,101 of them on the 2024 rolls were deleted—about two-and-a-half times the statewide average.The study found that electors with Islamic names constituted 14.6% of all deletions, compared with an estimated 12.1% share based on the Census 2011. After controlling for age and constituency, their odds of being classified as already enrolled elsewhere, rather than dead, were over two-fold those of other electors. The researchers said religion was estimated through a name-based statistical classifier and was not an attribute recorded by ECI. articles.title: Capital devpt meeting decides to fast track NH 66 works and to secure Centre’s nod for Thiruvananthapuram ORR
articles.summary: Thiruvananthapuram meeting to fast-track NH 66 Kazhakkoottam works, fix drainage, upgrade Enchakkal crossway, and seek Centre nod for Outer Ring Road.
articles.body: Thiruvananthapuram: Construction work on the Kazhakkoottam stretch of National Highway 66 is set to be expedited soon while a decision has been taken to pursue Union govt approval for the proposed Thiruvananthapuram Outer Ring Road (ORR) project within a month. The decisions were taken at a review meeting convened to assess the progress of NH 66 works between Enchakkal and Kazhakkoottam. The meeting was led by transport minister C P John, Thiruvananthapuram MP Shashi Tharoor and MLA V Muraleedharan. The meeting directed district collector Anju K S to arrange fire and rescue services to clear blockages in the drainage system along the NH 66 stretch. The drainage issues have been among the concerns affecting the area. A major decision was also taken to improve the Enchakkal crossway by increasing the number of spans from five to 13 to ensure smoother and safer traffic movement. Instead of relying on earth filling for the approach road, the meeting decided to construct as many spans as possible. The move is expected to improve access to the proposed KSRTC depot at Enchakkal and ease traffic movement in the area. National Highway Authority of India (NHAI) regional officer A K Janpaz, the district collector and heads of various departments attended the meeting. Meanwhile, construction on the Kazhakkoottam-Kadampattukonam stretch of NH 66 had remained stalled for several months owing to shortages of construction materials and labour. Restrictions imposed by Tamil Nadu on transporting soil and rock from the state had affected the supply of raw materials required for the project. Nearly 70% of the construction work on the stretch has been completed. Pune-based RKC Infrastructures Pvt Ltd is currently executing the project after the previous contractor, RDS Projects Ltd, withdrew from construction activities. The contractor had earlier indicated that full-fledged construction activities would resume by the second week of Nov.Stay updated with the latest Thiruvananthapuram news. Download the TOI App.

articles.title: Israel releases reporter held for five days over 'foreign agent' suspicion
articles.summary: Israeli authorities on Sunday released Arab-Israeli journalist Abed Abu Shehadeh without charge after holding him for five days over an interview he
articles.body: Israeli authorities on Sunday released Arab-Israeli journalist Abed Abu Shehadeh without charge after holding him for five days over an interview he conducted with a former Israeli lawmaker in Qatar, a legal rights group said.Abu Shehadeh was arrested at his home in Jaffa, near Tel Aviv, on Tuesday night by more than a dozen police officers. He was detained on suspicion of having “contacted a foreign agent”, according to an AFP journalist who attended his court hearing.His interrogation by police and Israel's domestic security agency, Shin Bet, focused on a publicly available interview he had conducted with Azmi Bishara, a former member of Israel's parliament and founder of the Arab political party Balad, Adalah, the legal group representing him, said.The interview, published on the Arab 48 news website ahead of Israel's October 27 election, addressed the election campaign and Palestinian political issues. Bishara has lived in exile in Qatar since leaving Israel in 2007, after facing allegations of links to Lebanese militant group Hezbollah, which he denied.Abu Shehadeh's lawyers argued that the interview constituted legitimate journalistic work and that speaking to Bishara did not provide grounds for criminal suspicion. They also disputed the characterisation of the former lawmaker as a foreign agent.Adalah welcomed Abu Shehadeh's release but said it did not make his arrest any less unlawful.“The police raided his home at night. He was interrogated about his journalism,” the group said, adding that the case sent a message that a public conversation with a political figure could lead to detention.Following his release, Abu Shehadeh described his detention as “wrongful” and “completely baseless”. He accused the Shin Bet of conducting a “witch hunt” on behalf of Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu, alleging that the investigation was intended to intimidate Arab citizens and undermine their political participation.“Arab society has chosen to struggle through democratic means, and no persecution will succeed in silencing us,” he said.The arrest came amid heightened political tensions surrounding Israel's Arab minority, whose members are descendants of Palestinians who remained in the country after its creation in 1948. Following the closely contested October 27 election, Netanyahu has criticised the prospect of Arab lawmakers helping the opposition form a government and alleged that they receive outside support.The detention drew criticism from press freedom groups and US lawmakers. Three newly elected Democratic members of the US House of Representatives — Brad Lander, Daniel Biss and Scott Wiener — wrote to Israel's ambassador to the US on Friday, urging authorities to release Abu Shehadeh or disclose the evidence against him and ensure due-process protections if charges were filed.The Committee to Protect Journalists had also called for his release, warning against penalising journalists for interviewing individuals critical of the Israeli government.It remained unclear whether the investigation against Abu Shehadeh had formally ended following his release. Israeli police did not challenge the decision to release him, leading to the cancellation of a further detention hearing scheduled for Sunday.You use AI every day. Now get your AI Quotient. articles.title: ED not ‘super cop’, can’t initiate PMLA proceedings through private complaints: Karnataka high court
articles.summary: Karnataka High Court rules ED can’t file private complaints to start PMLA proceedings without a predicate offence; quashes case against Nanje Gowda and others.
articles.body: Bengaluru: The Directorate of Enforcement (ED) cannot initiate proceedings by filing a private complaint under the Prevention of Money Laundering Act (PMLA), the high court has ruled.Allowing the ED to file a private complaint when the concerned govt authorities have deemed it inappropriate to initiate proceedings against an individual would effectively empower the agency to act as a ‘super cop’. Such an interpretation would run contrary to the legislative intent of the PMLA, which requires the existence of a predicate offence before the ED can initiate proceedings under the Act, Justice MI Arun observed in an order passed on Nov 6.“If the ED is permitted to file a private complaint, it would be in a position to file such complaints against any person on its own and initiate an investigation against them. This is not contemplated under the provisions of the PMLA,” the judge observed.The court made these observations while quashing proceedings initiated against K.Y Nanje Gowda, MLA from Malur and chairperson of the Land Grant Committee in Malur, Kolar district, and others.In the job scam case, the ED had conducted searches during which it reportedly found several documents relating to recruitments in KOMUL. Based on these documents, a separate complaint concerning the alleged recruitment scam was registered. The proceedings initiated by the ED were subsequently challenged through separate petitions.The court further observed that allowing the ED to proceed in such circumstances would effectively amount to presuming that the Lokayukta police or the concerned investigating agency had failed in its duty by not initiating criminal proceedings against the accused despite receiving information from the ED. This would place the ED on a higher pedestal, a position not envisaged by law.The scheme of the PMLA, the judge noted, contemplates that prosecution for the predicate offence must be initiated by the respective prosecuting agency or a third party, and not by the ED or authorities constituted under the PMLA.Consequently, the court quashed the proceedings arising out of the private complaint against Nanje Gowda, KN Gopal Murthy and C Raju Krishna. It quashed the Enforcement Case Information Report (ECIR) against YB Ashwathnarayan and C Raju Krishna.
